doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

title: The bass-playing friend Lenny Stewart arrested in Bermuda as a Communist
summary: The guitarist who loaned him money went to Bermuda as bassist and was arrested by two men; Appleyard met him again later in Sheffield.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Did you happen to work with either guitar players or piano players along the way that really helped you with understanding the chord changes and all that?
Yes, this fellow that loaned me the money in England, another interesting story. How’s your film, have you got — are you okay?
He loaned me this 15 pounds, and whilst I was in Bermuda the bass player left. So the band leader said to me, he said, “Do you know a bass player?” I said, “Well I know this

guitar player that plays bass. He’s a good guitar player and he’s not a bad bass player.” He said, “What kind of a guy is he?” Because they were always concerned about the personality of bringing somebody out all that way. I said, “Oh, I know him, he’s very quiet,” I said, “but he won’t cause any trouble.” He said, “Well all right.” So anyway, out he comes. And I used to do a lot of wandering around Bermuda. And I went to the movies once and it was a movie about, I think it was a “Third Man” theme or something or other, and “Oh” he said, “he’s not really like that.” And he was sort of critical of it. And anyway, I left to come to Canada. And shortly afterwards I left, one night they were playing on the bandstand and these two big guys came right in and said, “Are you Lenny Stewart?” “Yes.” “Follow us.” Handcuffs. Took him out. He was a roaring Communist. And he was trying to build a cell in Bermuda while he was there. They had been intercepting his mail. Talk about situations, huh? Anyway I never saw him — I think he went to jail. And some years after I was playing with Peanuts Hucko in England in Sheffield, and he walked in. I didn’t know what to say to him. He said, “Good to see you.” I said, “Yeah, how are you?”
Yeah. How’s the Communism going? Gee.
